data.hypothesis: The baseline averaged 3.494 μs; the prior valid flattened direct-global candidate averaged 3.278 μs, about 6.2% lower, but the catalog has only one distinct candidate and cannot establish which launch mapping is better. This experiment keeps 256 threads per block but maps them as 32x8, with contiguous x lanes in every warp, to test a practical row-tiled mapping against the flattened mapping. Direct loads avoid shared memory and barriers; the eight halo mappings exactly follow the baseline. No speedup is assumed before measurement.

memory_lessons.applicability: These are observed event-latency results for the supplied 64³ target; they do not establish why latency changed or which mapping is best.
memory_lessons.claim: The baseline was valid at 3.494 μs and the prior flattened direct-global candidate was valid at 3.278 μs. The catalog reports one distinct program, so launch-mapping comparisons remain untested.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this 32x8 warp-row mapping under the same correctness oracle and full-run event-latency protocol.

data.notes: The direct loads reproduce the baseline halo per offset: negative y indices below zero add my-1, and positive indices at or beyond my subtract my-1. This preserves the endpoint behavior rather than applying a conventional modulo to all coordinates. The launch covers the fixed 64x64x64 output without extra launches or allocations. This proposal has not been measured; correctness and latency remain for the controller to evaluate.
transformations: Replace the shared-memory stencil kernel with one direct-global output per thread and no block-wide barriers.
Use a 32x8 block and a 2x8x64 grid so each warp addresses contiguous x elements while retaining 256 threads per block.
Explicitly unroll all eight neighbor terms and reproduce the baseline y-halo mapping independently for every offset.
Write all 64³ outputs from the current A buffer on every call without extra allocation or launch.
